paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. This whole song is about where you plant your trust. The strong city isn't strong because of bricks. Its walls and ramparts are salvation, and the God who gives that salvation is, in the song's words, "the Rock eternal" (Isa 26:1, 4). So the song says, "Trust in the LORD forever," and the people who do get kept in "perfect peace" (Isa 26:3, 4).

Now, the song doesn't pretend life is easy. The singers waited, they were disciplined, and they cried out in pain, and I think some of that hurt could feel like it was going nowhere (Isa 26:8, 16, 18). They even say that all they accomplished, the LORD did for them (Isa 26:12). Baker, that is a lesson I had to learn the hard way, because my mustache LOVES to take the credit. The song also says the LORD shows His zeal for His people, and the fire set for His enemies will consume them (Isa 26:11).

And then comes the turn: "Your dead will live; their bodies will rise" (Isa 26:19). The pain doesn't get the last word, because God does. He tells His people to "Awake and sing," and He even deals with Leviathan, the fleeing serpent, in that day (Isa 26:19, 27:1). So trust Him today, friend. The Rock eternal is still the Rock when the night is long, and I'll be right here with the ovens warm, waiting on Him with you.
